member.name: T:ParticlesSample.Brazier
member.summary:
One brazier: the flame emitter on this entity, its embers and smoke on the children, and the light that flickers with them.
Stop(true) stops this emitter and every emitter below it. Stopping only ends the spawning: the flames, embers and smoke already alive finish their lives, so the fire dies down instead of vanishing. Play(true) lights it again.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.SpellCaster
member.summary:
The player's side of the arena: picks a spell, casts it where the mouse points, and toggles the arena-wide particle switches.
1-6 pick a spell P freeze every particle (Pause / Resume) Left click cast at the cursor T put the braziers out and light them (Stop / Play) Space cast at a random dummy G wind on the smoke and the rain (force over lifetime) B slow motion (Time.timeScale) R rain over the arena (Play / Stop)
The actions (Spell 1 ... Slow Motion) are defined in the project's input settings.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.WindAffected
member.summary:
An emitter the arena's wind pushes. SpellCaster toggles the wind; this adds it to the emitter's acceleration, on top of the acceleration the emitter was built with.
The acceleration bends where a particle ends up, and it is applied when the particle is born, so smoke already in the air keeps its path and the new puffs lean over.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.ArcaneVortexSpell
member.summary:
Arcane Vortex: two rune circles open and turn against each other, glyphs rise from the outer one, wisps and sparks spiral into the centre faster and faster around a growing column of light, then the vortex bursts outwards. Every cast opens a vortex of its own.
Shows: a pooled effect. The vortex is a prefab; each cast takes an instance from an EntityPool (Acquire places it at the target), drives it, and gives it back once its last particles have died (Release with a delay), so casts can overlap without spawning and destroying entities. Also: local simulation space (the wisps, the swirl and the core turn with the spinning instance, so a straight run to the centre becomes a spiral), rune circles that turn by their own rotation speed, and emission rates raised every frame while channelling.

member.name: F:ParticlesSample.ArcaneVortexSpell.releaseDelay

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.FireballSpell
member.summary:
Fireball: a projectile flies from the spell focus to the target and explodes.
Shows: emitters that move. The projectile's core and its rolling body simulate in local space and stay on it; its flames, smoke and embers simulate in world space and stay behind as a trail. An emitter that moves spreads each frame's spawns along the path it covered that frame (temporal motion), so a fast trail stays continuous. Stop leaves the trail to fade out. The explosion layers burst emitters: a flash, a flipbook fireball that blends between its frames, rolling smoke that takes over from it, a smoke column, sparks and burning chunks bent down by gravity, a dust ring and a shock ring on the floor, a scorch mark with glowing embers in it, and falling ash.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.FrostNovaSpell
member.summary:
Frost Nova: ice shards burst out and stop, two rings of faceted ice crystals erupt from the floor, cold mist rolls out, frost spreads under it and snow drifts down. The crystals hold for a moment and shatter into shards and ice dust, and the dummies caught in the ring stay frozen until they do.
Shows: particles working with meshes. The crystals are a prefab of lit, faceted meshes that an EntityPool hands out, one instance per cast; the script lays the ring out, grows every crystal with an overshoot (inner ring first) and, at the shatter, emits shards and dust at each crystal's own position with EmitParams. Also: position easing (OutExpo shards burst out and stop dead) and horizontal billboards that lie on the floor.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.HolyLightSpell
member.summary:
Holy Light: a column of light comes down with thin rays flickering around it, sparkles fall through it and rise again, a golden circle turns on the floor, rings spread out, and the dummies inside it are healed.
Shows: vertical billboards (the beams stand upright and only turn around their own axis to face the camera; the pivot puts their bottom edge on the floor), several layers of one beam texture at different widths and brightness, short non-looping streams started with Play, a staggered burst from a coroutine, and Emit with a position for the heal marks that rise from each healed dummy.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.LightningSpell
member.summary:
Lightning: energy gathers on the floor for a quarter of a second, then bolts strike down the same channel three times. The impact flashes, a shock ring runs out, sparks spray and fall, arcs crawl over the ground, smoke and embers hang in the air, and the strike arcs on to the dummies nearby.
Shows: timing a layered effect from a coroutine; burst emitters fired with Emit; a sheet of bolt variants where each particle holds one random tile; short non-looping emitters started with Play; and EmitParams, which places a single arc particle between two points - halfway, as long as the gap, turned along it. Each layer faces the camera the way its shape needs: the bolt, its glow, the flash and the crackles at the strike are vertical billboards that stay upright from every angle, the rings, the scorch and the arcs crawling outward lie flat on the floor, and only round or volumetric things (sparks, embers, smoke) turn fully to the camera.

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.MeteorStormSpell
member.summary:
Meteor Storm: a burning sigil opens on the floor and a volley of meteors falls on it, one after another, each leaving a fiery ribbon and a smoke trail and blowing debris, sparks and smoke out of the floor where it lands.
Shows: the script launches each meteor once - one Emit with a position, a velocity and a lifetime on the rock (mesh particles) and on its glowing core - and the particles take it from there: they fly the exact arc gravity gives them and die where they meet the floor (collision kill). The core's collision event fires the whole impact through sub-emitters, with no script: a flash that lights the arena (particle lights), flipbook fire drawn on cutout polygons, rock debris that bounces and settles (mesh particles with a collision radius, raising dust at every bounce through their own sub-emitter), sparks that draw their own path (trail render mode) and bounce, embers that light the floor, normal-mapped smoke lit by the scene, rings and a crater. The ribbon, the smoke and the sparks behind a meteor come from a slot entity the script moves along the same arc: they spawn per metre travelled (rate over distance), so the trail stays even at any speed. A closing ring marks each landing point for exactly the fall time (Emit with a lifetime).

member.name: T:ParticlesSample.Spell
member.summary:
Base of the six spells. A spell's entity holds its effect as child entities, one emitter each; casting moves the entity to the target and fires the emitters.
The emitters come in three kinds, and the spells show all of them: - burst emitters: emission rate 0, so they spawn nothing by themselves. Emit(count) puts exactly that many particles out at the next update, whatever the play state; - short non-looping emitters (a lifetime of emission, loop off, auto play off so they wait for the cast): Play() runs them once; - looping emitters whose rate the script changes while they run. The burst emitters simulate in world space, so moving the spell to the next target leaves the particles of the last cast where they were.
